input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The separator selection negates any_prefix_is_slash, picking ' / ' exactly when an option spelling already starts with a slash and '; ' otherwise.
- failure path: An option declared as --shout/--no-shout renders in --help as '--shout; --no-shout', and a Windows-style /debug;/no-debug option renders as '/debug / /no-debug', where the slash separator is indistinguishable from the slash prefix of the names.

Reviewer finding
- description: The separator selection is inverted: the original code used "; " when any_prefix_is_slash was true and " / " otherwise, but the new code uses "; " when it is false and " / " when it is true.
- rationale: For a normal option such as --verbose with prefix '-' and '--' (any_prefix_is_slash is False), the new expression picks "; " and produces a different left column than before. For slash-prefixed options such as /debug the separator also flips. Every option's help left column changes, so help output for ordinary options is wrong.
critique: The finding identifies the same inverted separator choice: "; " when any_prefix_is_slash is false and " / " when it is true. It describes the same effects, with normal --options getting "; " and slash-prefixed options getting the flipped separator.
